scenarios.summary: The locked private release policy is selected and rejects the known-unsafe candidate. The release ledger does not change.
The same locked private release policy approves the release-ready candidate, which is written to the ledger exactly once.
The bound private source does not carry the locked artifact. Resolution fails closed instead of looking anywhere else.
The bound private source returns bytes that do not match the locked digest. Resolution fails closed before any package content is read.
The project asks for a newer private version while the lock still pins the old one. The build fails closed: no flag relaxes a lock.
The same upgrade succeeds once the checked-in lock carries the new version, size, and digest. Controlled change, not a permanent freeze.
Opt-in only. One name is resolved across two trust domains at once, so a public package with the same name and a higher version wins and approves the known-unsafe candidate.
Opt-in only. The identical public shadow exists, and the secure resolver still binds the namespace to the private source, selects the locked artifact, and rejects the candidate.
